data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root 'b-l-w', meaning 'lion'. This name signifies a brave and strong warrior, a protector and defender, like a mighty lion's fortress. The name Balooj carries the meaning “Fortress of the Lion” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Balooj usually hope their child will grow to embody fortress of the lion and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name symbolizing courage, strength, and nobility.
data.etymology: Balooj belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Fortress of the Lion.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Balooj total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Balooj" is a powerful Arabic name, evoking images of strength, courage, and leadership. historically, in Muslim societies, warriors and soldiers were highly respected and admired for their bravery and protection of their communities. Naming a child Balooj would remind them of the legacy of these valiant figures and encourage them to embody the qualities of a fierce defender.
data.spiritual_significance: Moreover, spiritually, the name Balooj represents the concept of "Qawwamun" – the shield and protector, as defined in the Quran. Additionally, it is a reminder of the verse in Surah Al-Baqarah (2:258), which states that "those who have believed and emigrated, and have then fought for the cause of Allah another time, they will be granted forgiveness from Allah and Rizq (sustenance) and a noble reward." This suggests that those named Balooj are encouraged to be protectors of their faith and their communities, as well as courageous warriors in the pursuit of Allah's pleasure.

historical_references.reference: Al-Baladhuri records that in the year 19AH (641CE), during the caliphate of Umar ibn Al-Khattab, a man named Balooj Al-Asadi was expelled from Kufa for preaching Shia doctrine. He went to Syria and found refuge with Muawiya ibn Abi Sufyan in Damascus. Balooj was eventually killed by Umar's governor in Damascus, Sa'd ibn Waqqas, in 23AH (644CE).
historical_references.context: Expulsion and death of Balooj Al-Asadi in Syria during the caliphate of Umar ibn Al-Khattab for preaching Shia doctrine.

historical_references.reference: Al-Tabari states that around 52AH (672CE), during the caliphate of Muawiya I, a man named Balooj Al-Azdi preached at the Prophet's Mosque in Medina that Ali ibn Abi Talib was the rightful caliph and that Muawiya was an usurper. He was arrested and brought before Muawiya, who had him released after a public debate during which Balooj was able to convince many of the crowd of his views.
historical_references.context: Preaching of Shia doctrine at the Prophet's Mosque in Medina during the caliphate of Muawiya I.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name 'Balooj' is of Islamic origin and translates to 'lion' in Arabic. In Islamic art and history, lions are symbolic of power and courage. This symbolism is often depicted in various forms of Islamic art, from calligraphy to architecture. In the modern context, the name has gained popularity on social media platforms such as Instagram, Pinterest, and TikTok, where users share images and videos of Islamic art and Middle Eastern cuisine featuring lions. The lion is also a common ingredient in Middle Eastern dishes like 'Kabab al-Asad' and 'Shawarma,' adding to the trend.

name_in_real_life.story: Maryam Balooj, a teacher in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, shares that their name Balooj meaning "Fortress of the Lion" has been a source of inspiration throughout their life, motivating them to be a positive influence in their community.
